exporter.title: Operations & Export Manager
exporter.orderHint: Check to include. Drag to set the order inside combined files.

order.label: Processing Order
order.help: Check an operation to export it. Operations combined into one file are cut top to bottom - drag to reorder them.

filename.label: Base Name
filename.help: Every exported file starts with this name, followed by the operation it holds, and a ZIP takes it too. Left empty, it is the name of the first operation in the list.

singleFile.label: Export as single file
singleFile.help: Combines operations that run on the same machine into one file, cut in list order. Needs two or more operations of one kind; stencils always export on their own.

splitDrills.label: Split drill files by bit
splitDrills.help: Writes one file per drill bit, for machines without a tool changer. Hole sizes cut by the same bit stay in one file, so this only appears for drill jobs that use more than one bit.

zip.label: Bundle files into one .zip
zip.help: Delivers every file in one archive named after the base name. Off: each file downloads on its own.

includeComments.label: Include operation comments
includeComments.help: Adds readable notes to each file: a comment per operation in G-code, a header block in SVG. Unavailable when the post-processor cannot carry comments.

verboseComments.label: Verbose comments
verboseComments.help: Adds each operation's tool, feeds, depths and deepest Z to the G-code header, so an old file reads without the project. G-code comments are always in English.

toolChanges.label: Insert tool change commands
toolChanges.help: Emits T and M6, plus tool length compensation commands, where a file switches tools. Needs a file that holds more than one tool number - turn on single-file export or give operations their own T numbers - and a post-processor with tool changes.

groupByTool.label: Group operations by tool
groupByTool.help: Reorders the combined file so operations that share a tool run back to back, overriding the list order. Needs single-file export and more than one tool number in the file.

optimize.label: Optimize path order (whole job)
optimize.help: Reorders paths to shorten travel between cuts. Turn it off to keep the generated order when tracking down an unexpected move.

exporter.laserPadding: Physical padding around the exported board bounds in mm
exporter.stencilPadding: Padding around the stencil bounds in mm

calculate.label: Calculate Toolpaths
calculate.help: Process the selected operations and generate the G-code preview based on the current order and settings.

drillTooling.title: Drill Tooling
drillTooling.empty: No drill features detected. Load a drill file and generate the drill strategy first.

help.size: Hole diameter, or slot width. On an Excellon file, hover the size to see its tool code.
help.features: How many holes or slots the row holds. Holes and slots of one size get a row each, so each can take its own strategy and cutter.
help.strategy: Peck plunges at each hole and at both ends of a slot. Mill rings out a feature wider than the cutter; one about as wide is cut in a single pass, a slot along its centreline and a hole as a plunge. Skip leaves the row uncut.
help.tool: Cutter diameter for the row. Empty uses the feature's own size. Changing it discards generated paths.
help.toolNumber: The T number that calls the row's cutter: its pocket or collet. Every row except Skip needs one; rows that share a cutter can share a number.
help.peck: Depth of each peck on a Peck row. With canned cycles it is the Q word of G83 and G73; on a post without them EasyCAM writes the peck loop itself. Empty uses the operation's Peck Depth. 0, or Canned Cycle None, drills in one plunge.
help.feed: Feed for the row's milling moves, in mm/min. Empty uses the operation's Feed Rate.
help.plunge: Plunge rate for the row's pecks and Z entries, in mm/min. Empty uses the operation's Plunge Rate.
help.rpm: Spindle speed for the row's cutter. Empty uses the operation's Spindle Speed.

notice.geometry: Holes and slots of one size get a row each. Give every row a strategy, a cutter and a T number; a skipped row needs neither. Changing a strategy or cutter discards generated paths; a T number does not.
notice.strategy: Peck depth per row. Leave it empty to use the operation's Peck Depth. Strategy, cutter and T number are set at the XY Geometry stage.
notice.machine: Feeds and spindle speed per row. Leave a field empty to use the operation's value. Strategy, cutter and T number are set at the XY Geometry stage.

indexed.axialMismatch: Faces see different axial model extents (low end varies {low:mm}, high end {high:mm}) - end walls will not line up around the part. Check the rotation axis and model orientation.

boardRotation.label: Board Rotation
boardRotation.help: Apply a rotation (in degrees) to all files around itself.

boardSize.label: Board Size
boardSize.help: The calculated total dimensions of all loaded files.

bottomLeft.label: Bottom-Left
bottomLeft.help: Preview the origin at the bottom-left corner of the board's bounding box.

bwMode.label: Black & White
bwMode.help: Render the canvas in black and white, ignoring layer colors.

cannedCycle.label: Canned Cycle
cannedCycle.help: Pre-programmed drill cycle. G83 (peck drilling) retracts periodically to clear chips.

center.label: Center
center.help: Preview the origin at the center of the board's bounding box.

combineOffsets.label: Combine Offset Paths
combineOffsets.help: Merge all offset passes into a single geometry. Reduces G-code complexity but loses individual pass control.

cutDepth.label: Cut Depth
cutDepth.help: Final target depth for all cuts, relative to the material surface (Z=0). Should be a negative value (e.g., -0.05mm).

cutSide.label: Cut Side
cutSide.help: Where the tool sits relative to the polygon outline. Outside clears material around the shape. Inside clears within. On Path centers the tool on the line.

debugPoints.label: Debug Points
debugPoints.help: Show all individual points in all geometry.

depthPerPass.label: Depth per Pass
depthPerPass.help: Incremental depth of each pass when using multi-depth cutting. Smaller = gentler on tool.

detectNesting.label: Detect Nesting
detectNesting.help: When enabled, shapes fully contained inside other shapes are treated as holes and subtracted from the outer boundary during offset generation.

drillMultiTool.label: Multi-Tool Drilling
drillMultiTool.help: Assigns a strategy, a cutter and a tool number per row of the drill table. Each hole size and each slot size gets its own row.

drillStepOver.label: Step Over
drillStepOver.help: Percentage of the tool diameter to overlap on each concentric milling ring inside oversize holes.

drillMultiDepth.label: Multi-depth Milling
drillMultiDepth.help: Mill oversize holes in several Z levels instead of one full-depth pass. Easier on small cutters.

drillDepthPerPass.label: Depth per Pass
drillDepthPerPass.help: Material removed per Z level while milling an oversize hole.

drillEntryType.label: Entry Method
drillEntryType.help: How the cutter enters an oversize hole. Helix spirals down and loads the tool gently; Plunge drops straight in and needs a center-cutting bit.

dwellTime.label: Dwell Time
dwellTime.help: Pause duration at bottom of hole (seconds). Allows chips to clear and reduces burrs.

startCode.label: Start G-code
startCode.help: Your own start block for this post-processor, added where its program starts. Each post-processor keeps its own, starting from its setup's. {{toolNumber}} becomes the first tool's number.

endCode.label: End G-code
endCode.help: Your own end block for this post-processor, added where its program ends. Each post-processor keeps its own, starting from its setup's. {{safeZ}} and {{travelZ}} become those heights, never below where the program ends.

entryType.label: Entry Type
entryType.help: How the tool enters the material. Plunge: straight down. Ramp: diagonal. Helix: spiral down.

feedRate.label: Feed Rate
feedRate.help: Speed at which the tool moves while cutting (mm/min or in/min).

finishStepover.help: Stepover percentage for the finishing pass. Lower values give a better surface finish.
finishStepover.label: Finishing Step Over

finishingPass.help: Adds a final light pass at full depth with reduced stepover for a smoother pocket floor.
finishingPass.label: Finishing Pass

fusionMode.label: Fusion Mode
fusionMode.help: Merge all overlapping isolation/clearing geometry. Required for Arc Reconstruction.

units.label: G-code Units
units.help: Sets the units for the exported G-code file (G21 for mm, G20 for inches).

grid.label: Grid
grid.help: Toggle the visibility of the canvas grid.

indexDwell.help: Pause after each index rotation, before the tool re-enters the material, so a belt-driven rotary can settle. Starts at the post-processor's value; servo or geared rotaries generally need none.
indexDwell.label: Index Settle Dwell

rotaryAxisHeight.label: Rotary Axis Height
rotaryAxisHeight.help: How far the rotation centerline sits above machine Z0. Every Z of a 4th-axis program is measured from that line, so this lifts it into the machine's frame. A 4th-axis export with Absolute Z0 is refused while it is empty.

indexedAxisOvercut.label: Axis Over-Cut
indexedAxisOvercut.help: How far past the rotation axis each face may cut. Opposing faces that stop exactly on the axis are tangent, not overlapping, so backlash or a touch-off error leaves a spine on the centerline. Leave empty for one tool radius; 0 stops exactly on the axis. This deepens the waste only - it never cuts into the minimum-radius drive stub, so you can set both.

indexedBlankWidth.label: Blank Width (Across Flats)
indexedBlankWidth.help: Distance across the flats of the raw blank. Leave empty to derive it from the model. Anything on the model that sticks out past the blank cannot be reached and is flattened, so raise this if the part is larger than you declared.

indexedCollisionGuard.label: Collision Guard
indexedCollisionGuard.help: Limits tip depth so the shank and holder cannot touch the surface. Needs cuttingLength, shankDiameter, holderDiameter and holderStickout on the tool record; skipped silently without them.

indexedCrossFinish.label: Cross Finishing Pass
indexedCrossFinish.help: Adds a second finishing pass at 90 degrees to the first. Roughly doubles finishing time and noticeably improves the surface on curved faces.

indexedDepth.label: Carve Depth
indexedDepth.help: How deep each face may cut below the blank face plane. Leave empty to reach just past the rotation axis, which is as deep as one face can usefully go - anything further belongs to the opposing face. Set a value only to stop shallower than that.

indexedFaceCount.label: Faces
indexedFaceCount.help: How many flat faces to mill around the part. More faces approximate a round surface more closely but multiply machining time. Four suits a square blank, six or eight a pre-turned round one.

indexedRasterAxis.label: Raster Direction
indexedRasterAxis.help: Direction the finishing lines run on each face. Along the rotary axis gives long uninterrupted passes. Across the face suits parts whose detail runs around the part rather than along it.

indexedRoughStepdown.label: Roughing Stepdown
indexedRoughStepdown.help: How much depth each roughing layer removes on a face. Smaller is gentler on the tool and takes longer. Around a third of the tool diameter is a safe starting point.

indexedStartAngle.label: Start Angle
indexedStartAngle.help: Rotates the whole set of faces. Use it to line the first face up with a feature on the model, or to put the parting line somewhere you do not mind seeing it.

laserClearStrategy.label: Clearing Strategy
laserClearStrategy.help:
How the laser fills areas that need copper removal.

• Filled Polygon: Exports solid shapes - your laser software handles the fill pattern. SVG only.
• Offset Paths: Concentric paths shrinking inward. Most reliable for streak prevention.
• Parallel Hatch: Straight lines at a fixed angle. Fast but single-direction.
• Hatch: Perpendicular sets of lines. More passes shift the angle between each other.

options.filled: Filled Polygon - Laser software controls fill

laserClearingPadding.label: Clearing Padding
laserClearingPadding.help: Extra margin ablated around a copper region, beyond its own outline. Gives the beam room at the edges of a pour.

laserHatchPasses.label: Hatch Passes
laserHatchPasses.help: How many hatch passes to run. Each additional pass is rotated from the base angle, so coverage evens out instead of streaking along one direction.

colorPerPass.help: Automatically assigns a different color to each cutting pass. Useful for software that allows settings order to colors.
colorPerPass.label: Unique Color Per Isolation/Clearing Pass

laserCutSide.label: Cut Side
laserCutSide.help:
Where the laser kerf falls relative to the board outline.

• Outside: Laser cuts outside the line (board stays full size).
• Inside: Laser cuts inside the line (board shrinks by kerf).
• On Line: Laser follows the exact line (board shrinks by half the kerf on each side).

laserExportPadding.label: Export Margin Padding
laserExportPadding.help: Physical margin in mm added around the exported geometry. Gives the laser software breathing room for alignment.

exportDPI.label: Export DPI
exportDPI.help: Resolution of the exported PNG image. Higher DPI gives finer detail but larger file size. 1000 DPI is suitable for most PCB work. Match this to your laser software's engraving resolution setting.

exportFormat.label: Export Format
exportFormat.help: SVG exports vector paths that laser software (LightBurn, RDWorks) interprets with its own power/speed settings per color layer. PNG exports a raster image at the specified DPI - useful for direct image engraving modes.

laserHatchAngle.label: Hatch Angle
laserHatchAngle.help: Angle of the hatch lines in degrees. For parallel hatch, lines run at this angle. For cross-hatch, the second set runs perpendicular (angle + 90°). 45° is a good default - it crosses both horizontal and vertical traces.

heatManagement.label: Heat Management
heatManagement.help: Reorders passes so consecutive cuts are not adjacent, giving the material time to cool. Off emits paths in geometric order.

laserIsolationWidth.label: Isolation Width
laserIsolationWidth.help: Total width of copper to ablate around traces, measured from the trace edge outward. The number of laser passes is automatically calculated from this value, the spot size, and the step-over percentage.

laserLinesPerCm.help: Number of laser passes per centimetre. Higher values produce denser coverage.
laserLinesPerCm.label: Lines per cm

laserLinesPerInch.help: Number of laser passes per inch. Higher values produce denser coverage.
laserLinesPerInch.label: Lines per Inch

activeProfile.label: Laser Software
activeProfile.help: The program you will open the exported file in. It decides how layers are grouped, whether colors encode passes, and which palette is used.

reverseCutOrder.label: Reverse Cut Order
reverseCutOrder.help: Emit layers last-to-first. Needed where the importer processes the file bottom-up, so the intended first cut ends up first.

laserSpacingMode.help: Choose how to define the distance between consecutive laser passes. Step Over uses a percentage of spot size. Lines/cm and LPI set the density directly.
laserSpacingMode.label: Pass Spacing Mode

laserSpotSize.label: Laser Spot Size
laserSpotSize.help: Read-only reminder of the spot size set in Machine Settings, where it is changed. Offset and hatch strategies space their passes from it.

spotSize.label: Laser Spot Size
spotSize.help: The effective cut width of your laser beam. Manufacturer should list it in the specification sheet. Typical values: UV laser 0.02-0.08mm, Fiber laser 0.03-0.15mm.

layerColors.label: Layer Colors
layerColors.help: Color assigned to each operation type in the exported file. Most laser software maps color to a cut setting.

lineNumbers.label: Line Numbers (N)
lineNumbers.help: Prefix G-code blocks with line numbers (N10, N20…). Shown only when the post-processor's control accepts them.

lineNumberStep.label: Line Number Step
lineNumberStep.help: Increment gap between consecutive line numbers (N words). A step of 10 outputs N10, N20, N30… leaving space to insert manual blocks at the machine controller.

laserStepOver.label: Step Over
laserStepOver.help: Percentage of the spot diameter that adjacent paths overlap. Lower values (more overlap) give better copper removal but increase processing time. 50% is a good starting point; reduce to 30% if streaks appear.

svgGrouping.label: SVG Grouping
svgGrouping.help: How paths are grouped in the file. Your laser software decides what it can read: some import layers, some groups, some only color.

millHoles.label: Mill Holes
millHoles.help: If checked, generates circular milling paths inside any drill holes larger than the tool. If unchecked, generates a simple peck/drill at the center.

mirrorGeometry.help: Invert file geometry. Useful with bottom-layer isolation.
mirrorGeometry.label: Mirror Geometry

multiDepth.label: Multi-depth Cutting
multiDepth.help: Enable multiple passes at different depths for deep cuts. Reduces tool stress.

offsets.label: Offsets
offsets.help: Show/hide the calculated offset geometry. This is automatically hidden when a Preview is generated.

originOffset.label: Origin Offset
originOffset.help: Set a new X/Y origin. Click 'Apply Origin' to save this position as the new (0,0).

passes.label: Number of Passes
passes.help: Number of offset passes to create. More passes clear more copper but take longer.

thickness.label: Stock Thickness
thickness.help: The total thickness of your stock material. Used for cutout depth calculations.

thicknessCopper.label: Copper Thickness
thicknessCopper.help: Copper foil thickness, typically 0.035mm for 1oz. Used for isolation depth suggestions.

margin.label: Fit Margin
margin.help: Clearance added around the geometry when using Fit to Object.

material.label: Material
material.help: Stock material. Used for feed and speed suggestions; it does not change any generated coordinate.

zeroReference.label: Z Zero Reference
zeroReference.help: Where Z0 sits. 'Material Surface' means you zero on top of the stock; 'Machine Bed' means you zero on the spoilboard and depths are measured from there.

coolant.label: Coolant
coolant.help: Coolant the program switches on at its start and off at its end: mist or flood, in the post's own codes (M7/M8 and M9 on most posts). None leaves coolant to the operator.

vacuum.label: Vacuum
vacuum.help: Switches the vacuum or dust extraction on at the start of the program and off at its end, in the post's own codes (M10/M11 on most posts, M331/M332 on Makera, an auxiliary output on WinPC-NC).

peckDepth.label: Peck Depth
peckDepth.help: Depth of each peck before the bit retracts to clear chips. With canned cycles it is the Q word of G83 and G73; on a post without them EasyCAM writes the peck loop itself. 0, or Canned Cycle None, drills in one plunge. A Drill Tooling row can set its own.

plungeRate.label: Plunge Rate
plungeRate.help: Speed at which the tool descends into material (mm/min or in/min). Usually slower than feed rate.

pocketStrategy.help: How the pocket interior is cleared. Concentric Offsets shrinks inward in passes. Raster sweeps back and forth in straight lines.
pocketStrategy.label: Pocket Strategy

postProcessor.label: Post-Processor
postProcessor.help: Selects the setup for your CNC controller: the G-code it writes and the values these settings start from. A setup can also lock some of them.

preprocessed.label: Preprocessed
preprocessed.help: Shows the geometry *after* fusion but *before* arc reconstruction. Requires Fusion Mode.

previews.label: Previews
previews.help: Show/hide the toolpath previews, which represent the actual path of the tool.

rapidFeed.label: Rapid Feed
rapidFeed.help: The feed rate (mm/min) for G0 rapid movements (travel and safe Z moves).

rasterAngle.help: Angle of the sweep lines for raster pocketing. 0° is horizontal, 90° vertical, 45° diagonal.
rasterAngle.label: Raster Angle

rasterBidirectional.help: When checked the tool cuts in both directions. When unchecked it lifts and returns after each line for climb-only cutting.
rasterBidirectional.label: Bidirectional Raster

optimizeToolpath.label: Optimize Toolpaths
optimizeToolpath.help: Reorder and simplify the finished toolpath to cut travel time. Turn it off to keep the paths in exactly the order they were generated.

reliefBoundaryMm.label: Boundary Extension
reliefBoundaryMm.help: How far past the silhouette the boundary is formed. Used by Roll Over and Extend.

reliefBoundaryMode.label: Silhouette Boundary
reliefBoundaryMode.help: What happens at the model's silhouette. Stop leaves the surrounding stock. Roll Over forms a wall down past the edge. Extend keeps cutting a set distance beyond it.

reliefCellSize.label: Grid Cell Size
reliefCellSize.help: Sampling grid pitch in mm. Leave empty to derive it from the model size and the resolution cap below.

reliefCornerRadius.label: Corner Radius
reliefCornerRadius.help: Corner radius of a bull-nose cutter. Ignored for ball and flat tips.

reliefCrossFinish.label: Cross Finishing Pass
reliefCrossFinish.help: Adds a second finishing pass at 90 degrees to the first. Roughly doubles finishing time and noticeably improves curved surfaces.

reliefDepth.label: Carve Depth
reliefDepth.help: Total carve depth below the surface. Leave empty to use the model's own height.

reliefDepthMapping.label: Depth Mapping
reliefDepthMapping.help: Scaled stretches the model's height range to fit the carve depth - use it for artwork. Literal keeps the model's real millimeters - use it for dimensioned parts.

reliefFinishStepoverPct.label: Finishing Stepover
reliefFinishStepoverPct.help: Sideways step between finishing passes, as a percentage of tool diameter. Lower is smoother and slower.

reliefGridMaxDim.label: Auto Grid Resolution
reliefGridMaxDim.help: Cap on the derived grid's longest side. Higher captures finer detail and costs slicing time and memory.

reliefInvert.label: Invert (Mold Mode)
reliefInvert.help: Cuts the negative of the model, so the result is a mold of it.

reliefMaskUncovered.label: Limit to Model Footprint
reliefMaskUncovered.help: Only cuts where the model actually sits. Leave it off to clear the whole grid down to the floor.

reliefMinSegmentLength.label: Min Roughing Segment
reliefMinSegmentLength.help: Drops roughing segments shorter than this. Removes stutter without changing the cut.

reliefMode.label: Pass
reliefMode.help: Roughing removes bulk in flat layers, finishing rasters the surface. Both runs one after the other with the same tool.

reliefRasterAxis.label: Raster Direction
reliefRasterAxis.help: Direction the passes sweep. Run them across the model's long details rather than along them.

reliefRoughStepdown.label: Roughing Stepdown
reliefRoughStepdown.help: Z depth removed per roughing layer.

reliefRoughStepoverPct.label: Roughing Stepover
reliefRoughStepoverPct.help: Sideways step between roughing passes, as a percentage of tool diameter.

reliefRoughStock.label: Finishing Allowance
reliefRoughStock.help: Material left on the surface for the finishing pass to take off.

reliefSimplifyTolerance.label: Path Simplification
reliefSimplifyTolerance.help: Maximum deviation allowed when straightening finishing paths. Larger values give smaller G-code.

reliefSkipFloor.label: Skip Flat Floor
reliefSkipFloor.help: Skips the flat floor pass. Safe when roughing already clears the floor with the same tool.

reliefStartDepth.label: Start Depth
reliefStartDepth.help: Depth of the surface the relief starts from. Use it to carve inside an existing pocket floor.

reliefToolShape.label: Tool Tip Shape
reliefToolShape.help: Tip geometry the compensator models. Ball follows curves best, flat is faster on shallow relief, bull nose is a flat with a corner radius.

resetRotation.label: Reset Rotation
resetRotation.help: Resets the board rotation to 0 without changing the origin position.

resetUnsaved.label: Reset Unsaved Changes
resetUnsaved.help: Discards any unsaved origin offset changes and reverts to the last saved origin.

retractHeight.label: Retract Height
retractHeight.help: Height to retract to between holes. Should clear board but minimize travel time.

rolandModel.help: Select your Roland machine. Its steps per mm, feed limits, spindle control and start and end sequences come from the setup's model table; a machine the table lacks needs a custom setup with a model of its own.
rolandModel.label: Machine Model

notes.mdx15: Serial interface requires hardware flow control (RTS/CTS). Use an FTDI-based USB-to-serial adapter for reliable handshaking.
notes.mdx20: Serial interface requires hardware flow control (RTS/CTS).
notes.imodela: Low rigidity - use conservative feed rates for PCB work.
notes.srm20: VPanel rejects RML with syntax errors. RML mode has 0.01mm resolution; NC Code mode offers 0.001mm for ultra-fine work.
notes.egx350: High spindle speed - excellent for PCB isolation with V-bits.
notes.custom: Custom configuration - verify every parameter against your machine manual.

rolandZMode.help: 3D mode uses the Z command for simultaneous XYZ interpolation (MDX-40A and above). 2.5D mode uses PU/PD which only supports XY cutting at a fixed depth set by !PZ.
rolandZMode.label: Z Command Mode

rotaryAxis.label: Machine Rotary Axis
rotaryAxis.help: Which machine axis the rotary turns about: X gives an A word, Y a B word. It is how the rotary is mounted, so every 4th-axis operation uses it, and changing it marks them for regeneration. Only words the post-processor declares can be exported.

rotaryChuckSide.label: Chuck Side
rotaryChuckSide.help: Which end of the rotary axis the chuck holds. Each operation's chuck-end boundary settings apply at that end, and its tail-end ones at the other.

rotaryGrid.label: Grid in 4th-Axis View
rotaryGrid.help: Draws the ground grid in the 3D view's 4th-axis scene at the program's Z0: the rotation centerline, with Absolute Z0 the bed (the rotary axis height below the centerline), and on the axis-replacement route the top of the blank. Display only.

rotaryWorkholding.label: Chuck and Tailstock
rotaryWorkholding.help: Draws a simplified chuck in the 3D view's 4th-axis scene at the end of the part the chuck holds, and a tailstock at the other end when the operation holds the part between centers. Display only.

rotaryBlankDiameter.label: Blank Diameter
rotaryBlankDiameter.help: Outside diameter of the raw stock. Leave empty to fit the blank to the model automatically. Setting it smaller than the model flattens everything outside it, so only reduce it if the stock really is smaller.

rotaryCellSize.label: Grid Cell Size
rotaryCellSize.help: Size of one sampling cell on the model surface. Leave empty to derive it from the resolution setting below. Setting it manually overrides that and can make generation very slow on large parts.

rotaryChuckEndMm.label: Chuck-End Offset
rotaryChuckEndMm.help: Moves where the chuck end of the model is treated as ending, along the axis. Negative stops short of the real edge - use it for a slanted base or a tangent slope your tool cannot enter cleanly. Positive machines further past it, turning the waste down to the minimum radius as it goes. Too large a negative value leaves nothing to machine and you will get a warning. On Roll Over and Taper this is the lip depth or cone length instead, and is always positive.

rotaryChuckEndMode.label: Chuck-End Boundary
rotaryChuckEndMode.help: What happens where the model ends at the chuck. Stop at geometry is the default and the reliable choice: the waste is turned down to the minimum radius and the tool stops at the part. Roll Over leaves a small lip around the edge, but only works on an end that is flat and close to square against the axis - a slanted, domed or off-center end will show a scalloped ring, and you will get a warning. Taper cones down to the drive stub instead of stepping.

options.stop: Stop at geometry (turned to the core)
options.rollover: Roll Over - lip (needs a flat end)
options.taper: Taper - cone down to the drive stub

rotaryCornerRadius.label: Corner Radius
rotaryCornerRadius.help: Corner radius of a bull nose tool. Only used when the tip shape is Bull Nose. Must be less than half the tool diameter.

rotaryDepth.label: Carve Depth
rotaryDepth.help: How deep to cut below the blank surface, measured as radius. Leave empty to follow the model down to its own thinnest point. Auto depth near the rotation axis makes generation very slow, so set an explicit value on tall models.

rotaryFinishPattern.label: Finishing Pattern
rotaryFinishPattern.help: Spiral is one continuous helix with a single entry and no witness lines, and is the best default. Along the axis suits parts with axial features. Around cuts closed rings and suits parts with rotational detail.

rotaryFinishStepoverPct.label: Finishing Stepover
rotaryFinishStepoverPct.help: Distance between finishing passes, as a percentage of tool diameter. 10% gives a fine finish. Larger values are faster but leave visible scallops.

rotaryGridMaxDim.label: Auto Grid Resolution
rotaryGridMaxDim.help: Sampling resolution along the longest dimension of the model, used when cell size is automatic. Higher captures finer detail and takes longer. 1024 suits most work.

rotaryHoldingMode.label: Workholding
rotaryHoldingMode.help: Between Centers assumes a tailstock supports the far end, so material past that end is protected. Chuck Only assumes the part is cantilevered and the far end is open air.

rotaryKinematics.label: Rotary Kinematics
rotaryKinematics.help: Radial turns the part continuously under the tool for smooth round surfaces. Indexed 3+1 rotates to a fixed angle, mills that face flat, then rotates again. Indexed needs a post with an A or B word; radial can also run on a machine with the rotary wired to the Y driver.

rotaryMinRadius.label: Minimum Radius
rotaryMinRadius.help: Radius of the drive stub the tool never cuts into: what a chuck grips and a tailstock center bears on. It is also the radius a Taper end cones down to. On Indexed 3+1 it applies as a cylinder about the centerline, so a value here is a hard floor on how deep any face can go near the axis - the default 2mm keeps a 2mm core no face will cut through. Set it to 0 for a free end you want to part right through.

rotaryMode.label: Pass
rotaryMode.help: Which passes to generate. Roughing removes bulk in constant-radius layers. Finishing follows the surface. Both runs them in order with a single tool.

rotaryRoughAxis.label: Roughing Direction
rotaryRoughAxis.help: Direction the roughing scanlines run. Along the axis suits long slender parts. Around the circumference suits short stubby ones and keeps the tool engaged more evenly.

rotaryRoughStepdown.label: Roughing Stepdown
rotaryRoughStepdown.help: How much radius each roughing layer removes. Smaller is gentler on the tool and takes longer. Around a third of the tool diameter is a safe starting point.

rotaryRoughStepoverPct.label: Roughing Stepover
rotaryRoughStepoverPct.help: Distance between roughing scanlines, as a percentage of tool diameter. 45% is a good default for roughing.

rotaryRoughStock.label: Finishing Stock
rotaryRoughStock.help: Material left on the surface by roughing for the finishing pass to remove. 0.3mm is a good default. Too little and roughing marks show through, too much and finishing works hard.

rotaryRoute.help: How the 4th axis reaches the machine. 'Rotary word' sends A or B and drops Y - the CAM does the wrapping - in degrees, or in millimeters of arc for a rotary calibrated in linear units. 'Axis replacement' keeps Y carrying millimeters of arc at the reference radius, for a rotary wired to the Y driver with steps/mm calibrated. Only routes your post-processor declares are offered.
rotaryRoute.label: 4th-Axis Route

rotaryStockShape.label: Stock Cross-Section
rotaryStockShape.help: Cross-section of the raw blank. Round starts cutting at the blank diameter. Square starts at the corner radius and turns the stock round on the way down, which adds roughing time but saves you pre-turning it.

rotaryTailEndMm.label: Tail-End Offset
rotaryTailEndMm.help: Moves where the tailstock end of the model is treated as ending, along the axis. Negative stops short of the real edge - use it for a slanted top or a tangent slope your tool cannot enter cleanly. Positive machines further past it, turning the waste down to the minimum radius as it goes. Too large a negative value leaves nothing to machine and you will get a warning. On Roll Over and Taper this is the lip depth or cone length instead, and is always positive.

rotaryTailEndMode.label: Tail-End Boundary
rotaryTailEndMode.help: What happens where the model ends at the tailstock. Stop at geometry is the default and the reliable choice: the waste is turned down to the minimum radius and the tool stops at the part. Roll Over leaves a small lip around the edge, but only works on an end that is flat and close to square against the axis - a slanted, domed or off-center end will show a scalloped ring, and you will get a warning. Taper cones down to the drive stub instead of stepping.

options.stop: Stop at geometry (turned to the core)
options.rollover: Roll Over - lip (needs a flat end)
options.taper: Taper - cone down to the drive stub

rotaryToolShape.label: Tool Tip Shape
rotaryToolShape.help: Shape of the cutting tip. Ball nose gives the smoothest curved surfaces. Flat leaves scallops on curves but cuts flats cleanly. Bull nose is a flat endmill with a rounded corner.

rulers.label: Rulers
rulers.help: Show/hide the rulers around the canvas.

safeZ.label: Safe Z
safeZ.help: Maximum safe height for rapid moves and tool changes (G0). Must clear all clamps and fixtures.

spindleDwell.help: Time in seconds to wait. Essential for high inertia spindles that need extra time to come up to speed.
spindleDwell.label: Spindle Dwell

spindleSpeed.label: Spindle Speed
spindleSpeed.help: Rotation speed of the spindle (RPM). Higher speeds for smaller tools.

spotDepth.help: Depth of the spot drill pilot hole.
spotDepth.label: Spot Depth

spotDrill.help: Plunge a shallow pilot hole at each location before the main drilling pass. Improves accuracy on curved or uneven surfaces.
spotDrill.label: Spot Drill

stencilAddRegHoles.help: Generates 4 circular alignment holes outside the board boundaries to help pin the stencil in place during manual application.
stencilAddRegHoles.label: Registration Holes

stencilExcludeDrillPads.help: Automatically removes stencil apertures that sit directly over through-holes to prevent solder paste from falling into the holes.
stencilExcludeDrillPads.label: Exclude Drill Pads

stencilExportPadding.help: Physical margin (in mm) added around the stencil geometry in the exported SVG. Provides breathing room for alignment on vinyl cutters and laser plotters.
stencilExportPadding.label: Export Margin Padding

stencilIgnoreRegions.help: If checked, ignores large copper pours and traces, only generating apertures for actual component pads (flashes).
stencilIgnoreRegions.label: Ignore Regions

stencilOffset.help: Shrinks (negative) or expands (positive) the stencil apertures. -0.05mm is a common default to prevent solder bridging.
stencilOffset.label: Aperture Offset

stencilMachine.label: Stencil Output
stencilMachine.help: What the stencil is cut on. Router mills the apertures and exports G-code; Knife cuts on the line with a cutter offset and exports a vector file. Changing this changes which parameters and stages the operation has.

stencilCornerRadius.label: Aperture Corner Radius
stencilCornerRadius.help: Rounds each aperture corner so a drag knife or vinyl cutter can follow it. A radius smaller than the cutter compensation comes out square, because a round cutter cannot cut a corner tighter than itself.

stencilRegDiameter.help: The physical diameter of the registration pins/dowels you plan to use.
stencilRegDiameter.label: Registration Hole Diameter

stencilRegMargin.help: How far outside the calculated board boundary to place the registration holes.
stencilRegMargin.label: Registration Margin

stepOver.label: Step Over
stepOver.help: Percentage of the tool diameter to overlap on each pass. 50% is a good default.

tabHeight.label: Tab Height
tabHeight.help: The thickness of the tab. A value of -0.5mm on a -1.8mm cut will leave a 0.5mm thick tab.

tabWidth.label: Tab Width
tabWidth.help: The length of each holding tab in mm.

tabs.label: Number of Tabs
tabs.help: Number of small tabs to leave uncut, holding the board in place.

tool.label: Tool
tool.help: Select a tool from your library. The tool's diameter will be used for calculations.

toolDiameter.label: Tool Diameter
toolDiameter.help: The tool's cutting diameter - the widest circle it cuts. On copper isolation and engraving this is seeded with the V-bit's effective width at required depth, because that is what the offset has to use.

toolLengthCompMode.help: Where the controller gets the new tool's Z length after a change. 'Controller tool table' assumes you have measured each tool into the control's offset table. 'H from T': the control takes the offset register from the T word. 'Measured at change time' means a controller macro probes the tool and owns Z, so no G43 is emitted. 'None' emits nothing and you re-zero Z on the new bit yourself.
toolLengthCompMode.label: Tool Length Offset

options.table-implicit: Controller tool table, H from T (Tn M06 G43)

absoluteZ.label: Absolute Z0
absoluteZ.help: Z0 is fixed on the machine - the bed - instead of touched off on the stock. Nothing may run below it, so set the stock's Z zero to the bed. 4th-axis programs are lifted by the rotary axis height. Programs that mix flat and 4th-axis operations, and the axis-replacement route, are refused for now.

toolNumber.label: Tool Number
toolNumber.help: The magazine slot, carousel pocket or collet this operation's tool sits in - the T word your controller will receive. If your machine has no tool changer, leaving 1 on every operation is safe.

travelZ.label: Travel Z
travelZ.help: Height above the board (Z=0) where the tool travels between cutting paths.

vbitAngle.label: V-Bit Angle
vbitAngle.help: The included angle of the V-bit. Common values are 60, 90, and 120 degrees. Determines cut width at a given depth.

vbitTipRadius.label: Tip Radius
vbitTipRadius.help: Radius at the very tip of the bit. 0 is a perfect point; a real bit usually has a small tip radius or flat.

vcarveCornerAngle.label: Corner Threshold
vcarveCornerAngle.help: Separation angle below which a medial branch counts as construction and is discarded. Raise it to drop more detail on curved outlines.

vcarveSampleSpacing.label: Boundary Sample Spacing
vcarveSampleSpacing.help: Step used to resample outlines before the medial axis is built. Lower it for very small text; it must be below the thinnest stroke width.

vcarveNoiseThreshold.label: Noise Threshold
vcarveNoiseThreshold.help: Discards medial branches whose clearance changes by less than this. 0 disables it.

vcarveMaxDepth.help: Maximum depth for V-carve cuts. Set to 0 for unconstrained natural depth (no flat floor). Set > 0 to clamp depth and generate flat floor loops for wide areas.
vcarveMaxDepth.label: Max Carve Depth

vcarveMinChainLength.label: Min Path Length
vcarveMinChainLength.help: Drops carve chains shorter than this. Removes specks left by noisy outlines.

vcarveStartDepth.help: Starting depth offset. Use to engrave below an existing pocket floor.
vcarveStartDepth.label: Start Depth

verboseDebug.label: Verbose Debug
verboseDebug.help: Show extended 'debug' messages in the status log and browser console. Requires a page reload to see startup messages.

wireframe.label: Wireframe
wireframe.help: Render all geometry as thin outlines instead of filled shapes.

less-experimental.label: {name} (Less Experimental)
less-experimental.note: Tested but not 100% confidence yet. Check the output before its first run.

experimental.label: {name} (Experimental)
experimental.note: Somewhat tested on a couple machines with good feedback. Double check the output before running it.

very-experimental.label: {name} (Very Experimental)
very-experimental.note: Barely tested on a limited number of setups. Expect problems and check the output before running it.

radioactive.label: {name} (Radioactive)
radioactive.note: Little to no testing. Dry-run the output first and proceed with Extreme Caution.

custom.label: {name} (Custom)
custom.note: Loaded from a custom file. Check its output before the first run.

extraKeys.other: {count} keys are not in en.json and are ignored: {keys}

pluralForms.other: {count} plurals lack forms this language uses ({forms}) and show other there: {keys}

rules.toolChangeSwap: {path}: supportsToolChange needs useM6 or pauseAfterToolChange, or a tool change would write no swap at all.
rules.useM6NeedsToolChange: {path}: useM6 acts only with supportsToolChange. For an M6 on the first tool alone, use initialToolUsesM6.
rules.lengthCompNeedsSwap: {path}: tool length modes other than none need supportsToolChange and useM6. The first tool gets its G43 through the M6 swap, and probe relies on the control's M6 macro.
rules.rotaryWords: {path}: the a-word and a-linear routes need at least one entry in rotary.axisWords.
rules.rotaryRouteDefault: {path}: a setup that declares rotary routes needs defaults.rotaryRoute, one of them.
rules.defaultInOptions: {path}: default must be one of the options.
